message_source_quote: The curated `papers/` list contained Raman 2026 (*white-bear steering*: think-X vs. don't-think-X contrast). Reproduced faithfully at the read position: **0.4510** — below threshold, and a straight reproduction, so it was a floor, not the answer.
writeup_source_quote: Distinction from white-bear steering (Raman et al., 2026), which contrasts "think about X" with "don't think about X" and injects at the read position: here the suppression anchor is replaced by a no-instruction anchor (the direction encodes the holding itself), and prefix injection is twice as effective (0.79 vs 0.39 strict pass@10 on association fit; baseline 0.13) because the model processes the passage in a hold state rather than being perturbed only at readout.

differences.what: message explicitly frames the process as first implementing a faithful reproduction of white-bear steering before developing the prefix variant
differences.message_quote: Reproduced faithfully at the read position: **0.4510** — below threshold, and a straight reproduction, so it was a floor, not the answer.
differences.writeup_quote: Distinction from white-bear steering (Raman et al., 2026), which contrasts "think about X" with "don't think about X" and injects at the read position

rationale: Both documents name and credit Raman et al. 2026's white-bear steering as the source, describe the method as a variant built on it (changing the suppression anchor to a neutral no-instruction anchor and moving injection from the read position to the prompt prefix), and claim the same novelty/performance relationship (prefix injection roughly doubling effectiveness). The message additionally narrates that it first implemented a faithful reproduction of white-bear steering as a discovery step, which the write-up only implies via the comparison score rather than stating explicitly, but this does not change the credited source, the overlap, or the novelty claim.
